scope: Leviticus 18–20, all 94 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Leviticus 18–20. Complete original XML records include annotation notes at 18:17, 19:1 and 20:2; no numbering shift occurs in this batch.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Makes the speech introduction idiomatic while keeping Moses as recipient; the sentence continues into verse 2.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Separates the instruction to Moses from the divine message and marks the nested speech clearly.
verses.before: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: I am the LORD your God.
verses.after: “Speak to the Israelites. Tell them: ‘I am the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: I am the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Preserves both lands and the lived/bringing contrast; renders walking in statutes as living by them without omitting the repeated prohibition.
verses.before: You will not do as they do in the land of Egypt, where you lived, and you will not do as they do in the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you. You will not walk in their statutes.
verses.after: Do not follow the practices of Egypt, where you lived, or the practices of Canaan, where I am bringing you. Do not live by their statutes.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not do as they do in the land of Egypt, where you lived, and you shall not do as they do in the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you. You shall not walk in their statutes.

verses.rationale: Retains the paired legal terms and walking idiom in a readable participial phrase, with the full divine refrain.
verses.before: You will do my ordinances and keep my statutes, walking in them. I am the LORD your God.
verses.after: Carry out my ordinances and keep my statutes, living by them. I am the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall do my ordinances and keep my statutes, walking in them. I am the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Generic adam becomes whoever; retains live by them without adding eternal life, prosperity or a doctrinal account of obedience.
verses.before: You will keep my statutes and my ordinances; the person who does them will live by them. I am the LORD.
verses.after: Keep my statutes and my ordinances. Whoever carries them out will live by them. I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall keep my statutes and my ordinances; the person who does them shall live by them. I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the sexual sense of uncover nakedness and the male-addressed kinship list; the Hebrew image is documented and retained where it links relatives in subsequent verses.
verses.before: None of you will approach a close relative to uncover nakedness. I am the LORD.
verses.after: No man among you may approach a close relative for sexual relations. I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: None of you shall approach a close relative to uncover nakedness. I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves both parental expressions rather than silently making the first dependent on the second; renders the final euphemism explicitly and notes the possible explanatory connection.
verses.before: You will not uncover the nakedness of your father or the nakedness of your mother. She is your mother; you will not uncover her nakedness.
verses.after: Do not uncover your father's nakedness or your mother's nakedness. She is your mother; you must not have sexual relations with her.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father or the nakedness of your mother. She is your mother; you shall not uncover her nakedness.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the act while preserving the source's identification with the father's nakedness; does not reduce father's wife to biological mother.
verses.before: You will not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife; it is your father’s nakedness.
verses.after: Do not have sexual relations with your father's wife. Her nakedness is your father's nakedness.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife; it is your father’s nakedness.

verses.rationale: Unpacks the kinship alternatives without turning birthplace into legitimacy or shared upbringing; either reflects the source's plural ending.
verses.before: You will not uncover the nakedness of your sister, your father’s daughter or your mother’s daughter, whether born in the household or born elsewhere.
verses.after: Your sister may be your father's daughter or your mother's daughter, born within the household or outside it. You must not have sexual relations with either.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your sister, your father’s daughter or your mother’s daughter, whether born in the household or born elsewhere.

verses.rationale: Names both granddaughter relationships and retains the identification with the man's own nakedness rather than paraphrasing it as embarrassment.
verses.before: You will not uncover the nakedness of your son’s daughter or your daughter’s daughter, for their nakedness is your own nakedness.
verses.after: Do not have sexual relations with your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter. Their nakedness is your own nakedness.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your son’s daughter or your daughter’s daughter, for their nakedness is your own nakedness.

verses.rationale: Makes the kinship declaration the first sentence, preserving the born-to-father qualification so the rule is not generalized to every stepsister.
verses.before: You will not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife’s daughter, born to your father; she is your sister.
verses.after: The daughter of your father's wife, born to your father, is your sister. You must not have sexual relations with her.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife’s daughter, born to your father; she is your sister.

verses.rationale: Preserves the paternal-aunt relation and the flesh/kinship explanation in two clear clauses.
verses.before: You will not uncover the nakedness of your father’s sister; she is your father’s close relative.
verses.after: Do not have sexual relations with your father's sister. She is your father's close relative.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s sister; she is your father’s close relative.

verses.rationale: Keeps the maternal relation and explicit causal conjunction distinct from the preceding paternal rule.
verses.before: You will not uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister, for she is your mother’s close relative.
verses.after: Do not have sexual relations with your mother's sister, because she is your mother's close relative.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister, for she is your mother’s close relative.

verses.rationale: Retains the uncle's nakedness image and identifies his wife, not an unspecified biological aunt, as the second clause's referent.
verses.before: You will not uncover the nakedness of your father’s brother; you will not approach his wife. She is your aunt.
verses.after: Do not uncover your father's brother's nakedness. Do not approach his wife for sexual relations; she is your aunt.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s brother; you shall not approach his wife. She is your aunt.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated prohibition and explanatory relationship, rather than deleting the final repetition for style.
verses.before: You will not uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law. She is your son’s wife; you will not uncover her nakedness.
verses.after: Do not have sexual relations with your daughter-in-law. She is your son's wife; you must not have sexual relations with her.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law. She is your son’s wife; you shall not uncover her nakedness.

verses.rationale: Preserves the spouse relationship and linked nakedness, without inserting an exception or a living/dead condition absent here.
verses.before: You will not uncover the nakedness of your brother’s wife; it is your brother’s nakedness.
verses.after: Do not have sexual relations with your brother's wife. Her nakedness is your brother's nakedness.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your brother’s wife; it is your brother’s nakedness.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes the woman-plus-daughter prohibition from taking either granddaughter; reads take as marry and identifies the pinned her-kin referent as the woman, without adding a different kinship category.
verses.before: You will not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter. You will not take her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter to uncover her nakedness; they are close relatives. It is depravity.
verses.after: Do not have sexual relations with both a woman and her daughter. Do not marry her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter for sexual relations. They are the woman's close relatives. This is depravity.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter. You shall not take her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter to uncover her nakedness; they are close relatives. It is depravity.

verses.rationale: Fronts the lifetime qualification and makes the rival-wife relation intelligible; retains literal sister rather than silently generalizing the phrase to every second wife.
verses.before: You will not take a woman together with her sister as a rival, uncovering her nakedness while her sister is still alive.
verses.after: While your wife is alive, do not marry her sister as a rival wife and have sexual relations with her.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not take a woman together with her sister as a rival, uncovering her nakedness while her sister is still alive.

verses.rationale: Names the menstrual condition directly and preserves the prohibition on sexual approach; no claim about moral guilt from menstruation is added.
verses.before: You will not approach a woman to uncover her nakedness while she is in the uncleanness of her menstrual period.
verses.after: Do not approach a woman for sexual relations during her menstrual uncleanness.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not approach a woman to uncover her nakedness while she is in the uncleanness of her menstrual period.

verses.rationale: Renders the semen/intercourse expression directly while retaining the neighbor's-wife relation and resulting uncleanness.
verses.before: You will not have sexual relations with your neighbor’s wife, becoming unclean with her.
verses.after: Do not have sexual intercourse with your neighbor's wife and become unclean through her.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not have sexual relations with your neighbor’s wife, becoming unclean with her.

verses.rationale: Retains offspring, giving, passing over and the name Molech; does not insert fire absent from this verse, and records the debated recipient/rite interpretation.
verses.before: You will not give any of your offspring to be passed over to Molech, and you will not profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
verses.after: Do not give any of your offspring to be handed over to Molech. Do not profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not give any of your offspring to be passed over to Molech, and you shall not profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves male, the comparison with a woman and the predicate concerning the act; does not add age, coercion, cultic restriction or a modern identity category.
verses.before: You will not lie with a male as one lies with a woman; it is a detestable thing.
verses.after: Do not lie with a male as with a woman. It is an abomination.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not lie with a male as one lies with a woman; it is a detestable thing.

verses.rationale: Preserves distinct male-addressed and female clauses, animal scope, uncleanness and tevel; makes the animal's action in the latter clause explicit.
verses.before: You will not have sexual relations with any animal, becoming unclean with it. A woman will not stand before an animal to mate with it; it is a perversion.
verses.after: Do not have intercourse with any animal and become unclean through it. A woman must not present herself to an animal for it to mate with her. This is a perversion.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not have sexual relations with any animal, becoming unclean with it. A woman shall not stand before an animal to mate with it; it is a perversion.

verses.rationale: Repeats all-these-things and nations while making both human defilement and divine expulsion audible.
verses.before: Do not make yourselves unclean by any of these things, for by all these things the nations I am driving out before you became unclean.
verses.after: Do not make yourselves unclean by any of these things. All these things have made the nations unclean, the nations I am driving out before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not make yourselves unclean by any of these things, for by all these things the nations I am driving out before you became unclean.

verses.rationale: Retains past narrative sequencing, the land's own wrongdoing and vomiting image; does not replace inhabitants with an ethnic label absent from this verse.
verses.before: The land became unclean, and I visited its guilt upon it, and the land vomited out its inhabitants.
verses.after: The land became unclean, so I punished it for its wrongdoing, and the land vomited out its inhabitants.
verses.tsw_comparator: The land became unclean, and I visited its guilt upon it, and the land vomited out its inhabitants.

verses.rationale: Makes emphatic you contrast with prior inhabitants, retaining equal prohibition for native-born and resident foreigner.
verses.before: But you will keep my statutes and my ordinances and will not do any of these detestable things, neither the native-born nor the resident alien who lives among you,
verses.after: But you must keep my statutes and my ordinances. Neither the native-born nor the foreigner living among you may do any of these abominations.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you shall keep my statutes and my ordinances and shall not do any of these detestable things, neither the native-born nor the resident alien who lives among you,

verses.rationale: Keeps the explanation in past tense and repeats all abominations and the land's defilement.
verses.before: for the people of the land who were before you did all these detestable things, and the land became unclean,
verses.after: The people who lived in the land before you did all these abominations, and the land became unclean.
verses.tsw_comparator: for the people of the land who were before you did all these detestable things, and the land became unclean,

verses.rationale: Makes the warning's condition and result followable while retaining the second vomiting comparison and singular nation.
verses.before: so that the land does not vomit you out when you make it unclean, as it vomited out the nation that was before you.
verses.after: Do not defile the land and have it vomit you out, as it vomited out the nation before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that the land does not vomit you out when you make it unclean, as it vomited out the nation that was before you.

verses.rationale: Renders the doubled generic doer as anyone, retaining any scope and cut-off penalty without specifying a mechanism.
verses.before: For anyone who does any of these detestable things—the persons who do them will be cut off from among their people.
verses.after: Anyone who does any of these abominations will be cut off from among their people.
verses.tsw_comparator: For anyone who does any of these detestable things—the persons who do them shall be cut off from among their people.

verses.rationale: Makes guard-my-charge idiomatic, preserves both prohibitions and closes both levels of speech after the full divine refrain.
verses.before: You will keep my charge, so that you do not practice any of the detestable customs practiced before you and do not make yourselves unclean by them. I am the LORD your God.”
verses.after: Keep the charge I have given you: do not practice the abominable customs followed before you, and do not make yourselves unclean by them. I am the LORD your God.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall keep my charge, so that you do not practice any of the detestable customs practiced before you and do not make yourselves unclean by them. I am the LORD your God.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the renewed speech boundary and recipient with a sentence continuing into verse 2.
verses.before: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves the whole assembly and reason for holiness, with explicit nested speech and direct imperative force.
verses.before: “Speak to all the congregation of the sons of Israel and say to them: You will be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy.
verses.after: “Speak to the whole Israelite community. Tell them: ‘Be holy, because I, the LORD your God, am holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to all the congregation of the sons of Israel and say to them: You shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy.

verses.rationale: Retains mother-before-father in the pinned text and sabbaths plural; revere conveys fear/respect without reversing parental order.
verses.before: Each of you will fear his mother and his father, and you will keep my Sabbaths. I am the LORD your God.
verses.after: Each of you must revere your mother and your father, and keep my sabbaths. I am the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Each of you shall fear his mother and his father, and you shall keep my Sabbaths. I am the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Keeps both turning and manufacturing prohibitions, the cast-metal specification and the full refrain.
verses.before: Do not turn to idols, and do not make for yourselves gods of cast metal. I am the LORD your God.
verses.after: Do not turn to idols or make gods of cast metal for yourselves. I am the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not turn to idols, and do not make for yourselves gods of cast metal. I am the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Reads lirtsonkhem as acceptance on the offerers' behalf, not merely free choice; keeps the peace-offering relation to chapter 7.
verses.before: When you sacrifice an offering of well-being to the LORD, sacrifice it so that you may be accepted.
verses.after: When you offer a peace sacrifice to the LORD, offer it in a way that will be accepted on your behalf.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you sacrifice an offering of well-being to the LORD, sacrifice it so that you may be accepted.

verses.rationale: Makes the two-day allowance clear without requiring consumption on both days; preserves the distinct third-day disposal rule.
verses.before: It will be eaten on the day you sacrifice it or on the next day, but what remains until the third day will be burned with fire.
verses.after: Eat it on the day you offer it or the next day. Anything left by the third day must be burned with fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall be eaten on the day you sacrifice it or on the next day, but what remains until the third day shall be burned with fire.

verses.rationale: Keeps piggul consistent with 7:18, avoiding a claim that spoilage is the sole reason for rejection.
verses.before: If it is eaten at all on the third day, it is an abomination; it will not be accepted.
verses.after: If any of it is eaten on the third day, it is a defiled thing and will not be accepted.
verses.tsw_comparator: If it is eaten at all on the third day, it is an abomination; it shall not be accepted.

verses.rationale: Separates guilt and cutting off while retaining the desecration rationale; uses the established bear-guilt wording.
verses.before: The one who eats it will bear his guilt, because he has profaned what is holy to the LORD, and that person will be cut off from his people.
verses.after: Whoever eats it must bear their guilt for profaning what is holy to the LORD. That person will be cut off from their people.
verses.tsw_comparator: The one who eats it shall bear his guilt, because he has profaned what is holy to the LORD, and that person shall be cut off from his people.

verses.rationale: Makes field margins and gleanings distinguishable to readers while retaining both prohibitions.
verses.before: When you reap the harvest of your land, you will not reap to the very edge of your field, nor will you gather the gleanings of your harvest.
verses.after: When you harvest your land, do not reap right to the edges of your field or gather what the harvesters leave behind.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not reap to the very edge of your field, nor shall you gather the gleanings of your harvest.

verses.rationale: Preserves grapes remaining on vines versus fallen grapes, both beneficiary groups, and the divine refrain.
verses.before: You will not strip your vineyard bare, nor gather the fallen grapes of your vineyard. You will leave them for the poor and for the resident alien. I am the LORD your God.
verses.after: Do not strip your vineyard bare or pick up its fallen grapes. Leave them for the poor and the foreigner living among you. I am the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not strip your vineyard bare, nor gather the fallen grapes of your vineyard. You shall leave them for the poor and for the resident alien. I am the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Gives the three prohibitions direct force and preserves reciprocal social scope without treating every term as the same offense.
verses.before: You will not steal, and you will not deal falsely, and you will not lie to one another.
verses.after: Do not steal. Do not cheat or lie to one another.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not steal, and you shall not deal falsely, and you shall not lie to one another.

verses.rationale: Connects false oath with profanation while preserving the switch from my name to your God's name.
verses.before: You will not swear falsely by my name, and so profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
verses.after: Do not swear falsely by my name and so profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not swear falsely by my name, and so profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains oppression and robbery separately and specifies the overnight wage deadline rather than generalizing to timely payment.
verses.before: You will not oppress your neighbor or rob him. The wages of a hired worker will not remain with you through the night until morning.
verses.after: Do not exploit your neighbor or rob them. Do not hold a hired worker's wages overnight until morning.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not oppress your neighbor or rob him. The wages of a hired worker shall not remain with you through the night until morning.

verses.rationale: Makes the stumbling object concrete and keeps deafness and blindness specific; retains the fear-of-God command instead of substituting a general kindness maxim.
verses.before: You will not curse one who is deaf or put a stumbling block before one who is blind, but you will fear your God. I am the LORD.
verses.after: Do not curse a deaf person or put something in a blind person's path to make them stumble. Fear your God. I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not curse one who is deaf or put a stumbling block before one who is blind, but you shall fear your God. I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves both prohibited biases and positive justice, rendering face idioms as favoritism and deference.
verses.before: You will not do injustice in judgment. You will not lift up the face of the poor or honor the face of the great, but in righteousness you will judge your neighbor.
verses.after: Do not judge unjustly. Do not favor the poor or defer to the powerful. Judge your neighbor with justice.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not do injustice in judgment. You shall not lift up the face of the poor or honor the face of the great, but in righteousness you shall judge your neighbor.

verses.rationale: Reads the difficult stand-on-blood expression as nonintervention in danger, retaining blood and noting the alternative of acting against a neighbor's life.
verses.before: You will not go about as a slanderer among your people, and you will not stand against the blood of your neighbor. I am the LORD.
verses.after: Do not go about slandering your people. Do not stand by while your neighbor's blood is shed. I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not go about as a slanderer among your people, and you shall not stand against the blood of your neighbor. I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Renders brother in communal scope and emphatic rebuke clearly; preserves the compressed guilt clause and notes the differing causal readings rather than imposing one.
verses.before: You will not hate your brother in your heart; you will surely reprove your neighbor, and you will not bear sin because of him.
verses.after: Do not hate a fellow Israelite in your heart. Speak frankly to your neighbor in rebuke, and do not bear sin because of them.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not hate your brother in your heart; you shall surely reprove your neighbor, and you shall not bear sin because of him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the familiar love command because it is clear and source-faithful, with both vengeance and grudge prohibitions and the people qualification.
verses.before: You will not take vengeance or keep anger against the sons of your people, but you will love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.
verses.after: Do not take revenge or hold a grudge against your own people. Love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not take vengeance or keep anger against the sons of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves all three mixtures and renders shaatnez generally here; notes the wool/linen parallel rather than inserting materials not named in this verse.
verses.before: You will keep my statutes. You will not breed two kinds of your livestock together; you will not sow your field with two kinds of seed; and a garment made of two kinds of material will not come upon you.
verses.after: Keep my statutes. Do not breed different kinds of livestock together, sow your field with mixed kinds of seed, or wear a garment woven from mixed materials.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall keep my statutes. You shall not breed two kinds of your livestock together; you shall not sow your field with two kinds of seed; and a garment made of two kinds of material shall not come upon you.

verses.rationale: Keeps enslavement, designation to another man and both unfreed conditions explicit; selects inquiry for uncertain biqqoret with punishment/compensation alternatives noted, and adds no assertion of consent.
verses.before: If a man lies sexually with a woman who is a slave designated for another man, but she has not been redeemed or given her freedom, there will be an inquiry. They will not be put to death, because she was not free.
verses.after: If a man has intercourse with an enslaved woman who has been promised to another man but has neither been redeemed nor granted freedom, an inquiry is required. They must not be put to death, because she has not been freed.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a man lies sexually with a woman who is a slave designated for another man, but she has not been redeemed or given her freedom, there shall be an inquiry. They shall not be put to death, because she was not free.

verses.rationale: Makes the male offender the actor and the ram the guilt offering; keeps LORD and entrance location without transferring liability to the woman.
verses.before: He will bring his guilt offering to the LORD, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, a ram for a guilt offering.
verses.after: The man must bring a ram as his guilt offering to the LORD, at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall bring his guilt offering to the LORD, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, a ram for a guilt offering.

verses.rationale: Preserves priestly atonement, male beneficiary and repeated sin-he-committed wording; retains forgiveness without declaring the woman guilty.
verses.before: The priest will make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before the LORD for his sin that he committed, and he will be forgiven for his sin that he committed.
verses.after: With the ram of the guilt offering, the priest will make atonement for him before the LORD for the sin he committed. He will be forgiven for the sin he committed.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before the LORD for his sin that he committed, and he shall be forgiven for his sin that he committed.

verses.rationale: Keeps the unusual circumcision image twice rather than erasing it as forbidden; the explicit eating prohibition supplies clarity and notes explain the metaphor.
verses.before: When you come into the land and plant any tree for food, you will regard its fruit as uncircumcised. Three years it will be uncircumcised to you; it will not be eaten.
verses.after: When you enter the land and plant a tree for food, treat its fruit as uncircumcised. For three years it is uncircumcised to you; it must not be eaten.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you come into the land and plant any tree for food, you shall regard its fruit as uncircumcised. Three years it shall be uncircumcised to you; it shall not be eaten.

verses.rationale: Retains fourth year, all fruit, holiness and praise without adding a location or recipient not stated here.
verses.before: In the fourth year all its fruit will be holy, an offering of praise to the LORD.
verses.after: In the fourth year, all its fruit is holy, an offering of praise to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy, an offering of praise to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps fifth year and the purpose/result phrase as increase of yield, noting the alternate sense of adding fruit to the available harvest.
verses.before: In the fifth year you may eat its fruit, so that its yield may increase for you. I am the LORD your God.
verses.after: In the fifth year you may eat its fruit, so that its yield may increase for you. I am the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the fifth year you may eat its fruit, so that its yield may increase for you. I am the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Leaves the short blood rule broad and notes literal over/on and possible ritual scope; preserves the pair of forbidden practices without inventing techniques.
verses.before: You will not eat anything with the blood. You will not practice divination or interpret omens.
verses.after: Do not eat with the blood. Do not practice divination or read omens.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not eat anything with the blood. You shall not practice divination or interpret omens.

verses.rationale: Makes the rounding action understandable while retaining head sides and beard edges; does not supply an unstated motive.
verses.before: You will not round off the hair at the sides of your head or destroy the edges of your beard.
verses.after: Do not cut the hair at the sides of your head into a circle or destroy the edges of your beard.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not round off the hair at the sides of your head or destroy the edges of your beard.

verses.rationale: Keeps dead-person scope attached to flesh-cutting and does not silently extend it to or exclude it from the marking clause; notes uncertainty over the exact marking technique.
verses.before: You will not make cuts in your flesh for the dead or put tattoo marks upon yourselves. I am the LORD.
verses.after: Do not cut your flesh for the dead or put tattoo marks on yourselves. I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not make cuts in your flesh for the dead or put tattoo marks upon yourselves. I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains parental agency, the daughter's exploitation and the personified land; does not add a temple/cultic limitation.
verses.before: Do not profane your daughter by making her a prostitute, lest the land fall into prostitution and the land become full of depravity.
verses.after: Do not profane your daughter by making her a prostitute, so that the land does not turn to prostitution and become filled with depravity.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not profane your daughter by making her a prostitute, lest the land fall into prostitution and the land become full of depravity.

verses.rationale: Preserves the joined sabbath and sanctuary requirements and the same fear/reverence root used earlier.
verses.before: You will keep my Sabbaths and revere my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
verses.after: Keep my sabbaths and revere my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall keep my Sabbaths and revere my sanctuary. I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Uses practitioner terms while documenting spirit/practitioner ambiguity; preserves both turning/seeking and defilement.
verses.before: Do not turn to mediums or spiritists; do not seek them out and so become unclean by them. I am the LORD your God.
verses.after: Do not turn to mediums or spiritists. Do not seek them out and become unclean through them. I am the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not turn to mediums or spiritists; do not seek them out and so become unclean by them. I am the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Keeps the gray-hair image and bodily act of standing, with honor and fear as distinct commands.
verses.before: You will rise before gray hair and honor the face of an old person, and you will fear your God. I am the LORD.
verses.after: Rise in the presence of gray hair, honor the elderly, and fear your God. I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall rise before gray hair and honor the face of an old person, and you shall fear your God. I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains residence and land qualifications and direct prohibition on mistreatment, using singular they for the generic resident.
verses.before: When a resident alien lives with you in your land, you will not mistreat him.
verses.after: When a foreigner lives with you in your land, do not mistreat them.
verses.tsw_comparator: When a resident alien lives with you in your land, you shall not mistreat him.

verses.rationale: Preserves equal native-born treatment and the same love-as-yourself formula as verse 18, grounded explicitly in Israel's Egyptian experience.
verses.before: The resident alien who lives with you will be to you as the native among you, and you will love him as yourself, for you were resident aliens in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
verses.after: Treat the foreigner living among you as one of your native-born. Love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: The resident alien who lives with you shall be to you as the native among you, and you shall love him as yourself, for you were resident aliens in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Makes the three commercial measures explicit and retains the judgment/justice connection to verse 15.
verses.before: You will do no injustice in judgment, in measures of length, weight, or quantity.
verses.after: Do not act unjustly when measuring length, weight, or volume.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall do no injustice in judgment, in measures of length, weight, or quantity.

verses.rationale: Preserves four repetitions of honest, both ancient units and the exodus identity clause; unit explanations remain in vocabulary.
verses.before: You will have honest balances, honest weights, an honest ephah, and an honest hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt.
verses.after: Use honest scales, honest weights, an honest ephah, and an honest hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall have honest balances, honest weights, an honest ephah, and an honest hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Retains both all quantifiers and keeping/doing, closing both levels of speech after the refrain.
verses.before: You will keep all my statutes and all my judgments and do them. I am the LORD.
verses.after: Keep all my statutes and all my ordinances, and carry them out. I am the LORD.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall keep all my statutes and all my judgments and do them. I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Marks a fresh divine speech addressed to Moses, continuing across the verse boundary.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains native/foreigner scope, offspring, death and the community's stoning action; no fire rite is inserted into the verse.
verses.before: “You will say to the Israelites: Any one of the Israelites or of the resident aliens living in Israel who gives any of his offspring to Molech will surely be put to death. The people of the land will stone that person with stones.
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites: ‘Any Israelite or foreigner living in Israel who gives any of their offspring to Molech must be put to death. The people of the land must stone that person.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall say to the Israelites: Any one of the Israelites or of the resident aliens living in Israel who gives any of his offspring to Molech shall surely be put to death. The people of the land shall stone that person with stones.

verses.rationale: Preserves emphatic divine agency, face image, cutting off and both sanctuary and name consequences.
verses.before: I myself will set my face against that person and cut him off from among his people, because he has given some of his offspring to Molech, making my sanctuary unclean and profaning my holy name.
verses.after: I myself will set my face against that person and cut them off from among their people, because they gave their offspring to Molech, defiling my sanctuary and profaning my holy name.
verses.tsw_comparator: I myself will set my face against that person and cut him off from among his people, because he has given some of his offspring to Molech, making my sanctuary unclean and profaning my holy name.

verses.rationale: Retains deliberate eye-closing and the execution omission, allowing the condition to continue into verse 5 in one paragraph.
verses.before: If the people of the land hide their eyes from that person when he gives his offspring to Molech and do not put him to death,
verses.after: If the people of the land close their eyes to that person giving offspring to Molech and fail to put that person to death,
verses.tsw_comparator: If the people of the land hide their eyes from that person when he gives his offspring to Molech and do not put him to death,

verses.rationale: Keeps family under divine opposition but does not automatically equate every family member with the followers who are cut off; retains the sexual metaphor.
verses.before: then I will set my face against that person and his family and cut him off, together with everyone who prostitute themselves after him by prostituting themselves after Molech, from among their people.
verses.after: I myself will set my face against that person and their family. I will cut off from among their people both that person and all who follow them in prostituting themselves to Molech.
verses.tsw_comparator: then I will set my face against that person and his family and cut him off, together with all who prostitute themselves after him by prostituting themselves after Molech, from among their people.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes consultation from the practitioners in verse 27, keeping the metaphor, face image and divine agent of cutting off.
verses.before: The person who turns to mediums and spiritists, prostituting themselves after them, I will set my face against that person and cut that person off from among the people.
verses.after: If anyone turns to mediums and spiritists, prostituting themselves by following them, I will set my face against that person and cut them off from their people.
verses.tsw_comparator: The person who turns to mediums and spiritists, prostituting themselves after them, I will set my face against that person and cut that person off from among the people.

verses.rationale: Retains self-consecration and holiness as two clauses, preparing the contrast with the LORD making them holy in verse 8.
verses.before: Make yourselves holy and be holy, for I am the LORD your God.
verses.after: Consecrate yourselves and be holy, because I am the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Make yourselves holy and be holy, for I am the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Preserves keeping and doing and renders the divine sanctifying participle as makes-you-holy without erasing its relation to verse 7.
verses.before: Keep my statutes and do them. I am the LORD who makes you holy.
verses.after: Keep my statutes and carry them out. I am the LORD, who makes you holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Keep my statutes and do them. I am the LORD who makes you holy.

verses.rationale: Retains both parental alternatives, the repeated offense and death responsibility image; does not weaken cursing to ordinary disagreement.
verses.before: Anyone who curses father or mother will surely be put to death. That person has cursed father or mother; their blood is upon them.
verses.after: Anyone who curses their father or mother must be put to death. They have cursed their father or mother; their blood is on themselves.
verses.tsw_comparator: Anyone who curses father or mother shall surely be put to death. That person has cursed father or mother; their blood is upon them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the pinned Hebrew's repeated adultery clause rather than following a shortened comparator reading; explicitly retains male and female penalty subjects.
verses.before: If a man commits adultery with another man’s wife, if he commits adultery with his neighbor’s wife, both the adulterer and the adulteress will surely be put to death.
verses.after: If a man commits adultery with another man's wife, committing adultery with his neighbor's wife, both the adulterer and the adulteress must be put to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a man commits adultery with another man’s wife, if he commits adultery with his neighbor’s wife, both the adulterer and the adulteress shall surely be put to death.

verses.rationale: Keeps the sexual act, father's-wife relation, father-linked nakedness and both-person capital penalty without adding consent qualifications absent from the verse.
verses.before: If a man lies with his father’s wife, he has uncovered his father’s nakedness. Both of them will surely be put to death; their blood is upon them.
verses.after: If a man lies with his father's wife, he has uncovered his father's nakedness. Both of them must be put to death; their blood is on themselves.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a man lies with his father’s wife, he has uncovered his father’s nakedness. Both of them shall surely be put to death; their blood is upon them.

verses.rationale: Retains the daughter-in-law relation and the repeated blood formula; tevel agrees with 18:23 without changing the specified persons into an abstract category.
verses.before: If a man lies with his daughter-in-law, both of them will surely be put to death. They have committed a perversion; their blood is upon them.
verses.after: If a man lies with his daughter-in-law, both of them must be put to death. They have committed a perversion; their blood is on themselves.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a man lies with his daughter-in-law, both of them shall surely be put to death. They have committed a perversion; their blood is upon them.

verses.rationale: Preserves male specificity, comparison, both participants and capital penalty without adding a modern identity label or an unstated restriction on context.
verses.before: If a man lies with a male as one lies with a woman, both of them have done a detestable thing. They will surely be put to death; their blood is upon them.
verses.after: If a man lies with a male as with a woman, both have committed an abomination. They must be put to death; their blood is on themselves.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a man lies with a male as one lies with a woman, both of them have done a detestable thing. They shall surely be put to death; their blood is upon them.

verses.rationale: Retains take and all three people in the burning penalty; does not repair the difficult rule by replacing the women with only the later partner, and notes marital/sexual scope.
verses.before: If a man takes a woman and her mother, it is depravity. He and they will be burned with fire, so that there may be no depravity among you.
verses.after: If a man takes both a woman and her mother, this is depravity. He and the women must be burned with fire, so that there is no depravity among you.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a man takes a woman and her mother, it is depravity. He and they shall be burned with fire, so that there may be no depravity among you.

verses.rationale: Keeps human capital penalty and the separately commanded animal killing rather than generalizing the result to punishment.
verses.before: If a man has sexual relations with an animal, he will surely be put to death, and you will kill the animal.
verses.after: If a man has intercourse with an animal, he must be put to death, and you must kill the animal.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a man has sexual relations with an animal, he shall surely be put to death, and you shall kill the animal.

verses.rationale: Preserves female and animal roles, the direct command and repeated death/blood formula, including the source's difficult joint scope.
verses.before: If a woman approaches any animal to mate with it, you will kill the woman and the animal. They will surely be put to death; their blood is upon them.
verses.after: If a woman approaches an animal for it to mate with her, you must kill both the woman and the animal. They must be put to death; their blood is on themselves.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a woman approaches any animal to mate with it, you shall kill the woman and the animal. They shall surely be put to death; their blood is upon them.

verses.rationale: Keeps both sibling alternatives, reciprocal seeing, public cutting off and final male guilt; interprets hesed here as disgrace, not covenant kindness.
verses.before: If a man takes his sister, his father’s daughter or his mother’s daughter, and he sees her nakedness and she sees his nakedness, it is a disgrace. They will be cut off in the sight of their people. He has uncovered his sister’s nakedness; he will bear his guilt.
verses.after: If a man takes his sister, his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and sees her nakedness while she sees his, this is a disgrace. They will be cut off before the eyes of their people. He has uncovered his sister's nakedness and must bear his guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a man takes his sister, his father’s daughter or his mother’s daughter, and he sees her nakedness and she sees his nakedness, it is a disgrace. They shall be cut off in the sight of their people. He has uncovered his sister’s nakedness; he shall bear his guilt.

verses.rationale: Preserves menstrual condition, the double fountain image and differentiated actors; does not silently replace the source with a generic impurity rule.
verses.before: If a man lies with a woman during her menstrual period and uncovers her nakedness, he has exposed her source and she has uncovered the source of her blood. Both of them will be cut off from among their people.
verses.after: If a man lies with a woman during her period and uncovers her nakedness, he has laid bare her fountain, and she has uncovered the fountain of her blood. Both will be cut off from among their people.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a man lies with a woman during her menstrual period and uncovers her nakedness, he has exposed her source and she has uncovered the source of her blood. Both of them shall be cut off from among their people.

verses.rationale: Preserves maternal-before-paternal order, explains the switch from second to third person and keeps plural guilt for the pair.
verses.before: You will not uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister or your father’s sister, for one who does so has exposed a close relative. They will bear their guilt.
verses.after: Do not have sexual relations with your mother's sister or your father's sister. A man who does so has laid bare his own close relative; they must bear their guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister or your father’s sister, for one who does so has exposed a close relative. They shall bear their guilt.

verses.rationale: Identifies aunt by marriage from the uncle clause and preserves die-childless rather than silently matching the following verse's be-childless wording.
verses.before: If a man lies with his uncle’s wife, he has uncovered his uncle’s nakedness. They will bear their sin; they will die childless.
verses.after: If a man lies with his uncle's wife, he has uncovered his uncle's nakedness. They must bear their sin; they will die childless.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a man lies with his uncle’s wife, he has uncovered his uncle’s nakedness. They shall bear their sin; they shall die childless.

verses.rationale: Keeps take open to marital/sexual possession, niddah's impurity sense and be-childless; does not insert an exception absent from the verse.
verses.before: If a man takes his brother’s wife, it is impurity. He has uncovered his brother’s nakedness; they will be childless.
verses.after: If a man takes his brother's wife, this is uncleanness. He has uncovered his brother's nakedness; they will be childless.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a man takes his brother’s wife, it is impurity. He has uncovered his brother’s nakedness; they shall be childless.

verses.rationale: Retains both all quantifiers, keeping/doing and the land-vomiting image, with clear purpose/result syntax and settlement language.
verses.before: You will keep all my statutes and all my ordinances and do them, so that the land into which I am bringing you to dwell does not vomit you out.
verses.after: Keep all my statutes and all my ordinances, and carry them out, so that the land where I am bringing you to live does not vomit you out.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall keep all my statutes and all my ordinances and do them, so that the land into which I am bringing you to dwell does not vomit you out.

verses.rationale: Preserves the pinned singular nation against pluralizing comparators, all-these-things and the force of divine disgust.
verses.before: You will not walk in the statutes of the nation that I am driving out before you, because they did all these things, and I abhorred them.
verses.after: Do not live by the customs of the nation I am driving out before you. They did all these things, and I loathed them.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not walk in the statutes of the nation that I am driving out before you, because they did all these things, and I abhorred them.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated possession, emphatic divine giving, milk-and-honey image and separation from peoples without adding all.
verses.before: Yet I have said to you, ‘You will possess their land, and I will give it to you to possess, a land flowing with milk and honey.’ I am the LORD your God, who has separated you from the peoples.
verses.after: I have told you: You will take possession of their land. I myself will give it to you as your possession, a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the LORD your God, who set you apart from the peoples.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I have said to you, ‘You shall possess their land, and I will give it to you to possess, a land flowing with milk and honey.’ I am the LORD your God, who has separated you from the peoples.

verses.rationale: Preserves reversed clean/unclean order for birds and the shared separation verb; clarifies that the final relative clause concerns the creatures, not the ground.
verses.before: So you will distinguish between the clean animal and the unclean, and between the unclean bird and the clean. You will not make yourselves detestable by animal or bird or anything that swarms on the ground, which I have separated from you as unclean.
verses.after: You must distinguish clean animals from unclean ones, and unclean birds from clean ones. Do not make yourselves detestable through animals, birds, or anything that moves along the ground, which I have set apart for you as unclean.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore you shall distinguish between the clean animal and the unclean, and between the unclean bird and the clean. You shall not make yourselves detestable by animal or bird or anything that swarms on the ground, which I have separated from you as unclean.

verses.rationale: Keeps holiness, divine self-identification and the purpose of separation, using the same set-apart wording as verses 24–25.
verses.before: You will be holy to me, for I the LORD am holy, and I have separated you from the peoples so that you may be mine.
verses.after: Be holy to me, because I, the LORD, am holy. I have set you apart from the peoples to be mine.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall be holy to me, for I the LORD am holy, and I have separated you from the peoples so that you may be mine.

verses.rationale: Preserves has-in-them wording and both sexes rather than merely repeating consultation in verse 6; retains stoning and the concluding blood formula with a note on practitioner terminology.
verses.before: A man or woman who is a medium or spiritist will surely be put to death. They will be stoned with stones; their blood is upon them.”
verses.after: A man or woman who has a spirit of the dead or a familiar spirit must be put to death. They must be stoned; their blood is on themselves.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: A man or woman who is a medium or spiritist shall surely be put to death. They shall be stoned with stones; their blood is upon them.”
